```{python}
import polars as pl
import numpy as np
from lets_plot import *
import polars.selectors as cs

LetsPlot.setup_html(isolated_frame=True)

data_url = "https://byuidatascience.github.io/DS250-Course-Polars/Data/StarWars_with_emails.csv"
```

<!-- Same load/cleanup as Task 1, carried over so this data prep task can run on its own -->

```{python}
a = pl.Series(pl.read_csv(data_url, skip_rows = 10, n_rows=1, has_header=False, encoding = 'utf8-lossy').row(0))
a[2] = "seen_any"

a = (
  a.str.replace(r".+seen.+", "seen_")
   .str.replace(r".+rank.+", "rank_")
   .str.replace(r"(.+favorably.+)", "fav_")
   .fill_null(strategy = "forward")
   .str.replace("�+", "")
   .str.strip_chars()
   .str.to_lowercase()
   .str.replace_all(" ", "_")
   .str.replace(r"location(.+)", "location")
)
a[3] = "star_wars_fan"
a[30] = "who_shot_first"
a[31] = "know_expanded_universe"
a[32] = "expanded_universe_fan"
a[33] = "star_trek_fan"
```

```{python}
b = pl.Series(pl.read_csv(data_url, skip_rows = 11, n_rows=1, has_header=False, encoding = 'utf8-lossy').row(0))

b = (
  b.str.replace(r"Star Wars: (Episode \w+) .+", "${1}")
   .str.replace("Response", "")
   .str.replace_all(" ", "_")
   .fill_null("")
   .str.strip_chars()
)
```

```{python}
new_names = (a + b).to_list()
df = pl.read_csv(data_url, skip_rows=12, has_header=False, new_columns = new_names )
```

```{python}
# email regex from Task 1, carried over
df_new = df.with_columns(
  pl.col("email").str.extract(r"^([a-zA-Z]+)", 1).str.strip_chars().alias("first_name"),
  pl.col("email").str.extract(r"[._\d]([a-zA-Z]+)@", 1).str.strip_chars().alias("last_name"),
  pl.col("email").str.extract(r"@(.+)$", 1).str.to_lowercase().str.strip_chars().alias("email_domain")
)
```

## QUESTION 1

1. __Clean and recode age, education, household_income, and the fav_ columns so they're ready for ML.__

```{python}
# only keep respondents who've seen at least one film
df_ml = df_new.filter(pl.any_horizontal(pl.col(r"^seen_Episode.*$").is_not_null()))
```

```{python}
# age to int
df_ml1 = df_ml.with_columns(
  pl.col('age').str.extract(r"(\d+)", 1).cast(pl.Int32).alias("age_int")
).drop('age')
```

```{python}
# education to int
df_ml2 = df_ml1.with_columns(
    pl.col("education").replace_strict({
        "Less than high school degree": 1,
        "High school degree": 2,
        "Some college or Associate degree": 3,
        "Bachelor degree": 4,
        "Graduate degree": 5
    }).alias("education_int")
).drop("education")
```

```{python}
# household_income to int
df_ml3 = df_ml2.with_columns(
    pl.col("household_income").str.replace_all(r",", "").str.extract(r"^\$([\d]+)", 1).cast(pl.Int32).alias("income_int")
).drop("household_income")
```

```{python}
# fav_ columns to numeric scale
df_final = df_ml3.with_columns(
    cs.starts_with("fav_").replace_strict({
        "Very unfavorably": 1,
        "Somewhat unfavorably": 2,
        "Neither favorably nor unfavorably (neutral)": 3,
        "Somewhat favorably": 4,
        "Very favorably": 5,
        "Unfamiliar (N/A)": 0
    })
)

display(df_final.head(5))
```
